title: finding: the security `explain` decision has an engine and an API but no UI anywhere — "why can this user see this record" is unanswerable from the product, while docs promise "audit and explain"
body:
## What was observed

While recording a permissions walkthrough against objectstack @ `ad217b1`, the nine-layer
`explain` decision was found to be **API-only**:

- `GET /api/v1/security/explain` returns a high-quality layered verdict (grants / narrows /
  widens across nine layers, with the deciding rule named at each layer).
- A repo-wide search across `console/`, `studio/` and `ui/` restricted to `--include=*.tsx`
  returns **zero hits for `explain`**. There is no panel, drawer, tooltip, inspector or
  developer affordance that renders that verdict.

So the question the feature exists to answer — *"why can this user see this record?"* — cannot
be answered by anyone working inside the product. It can only be answered by someone who knows
the endpoint exists and can issue an authenticated HTTP request by hand.

## Why this is being filed as a product finding

The capabilities documentation describes the permission model as **"audit and explain"**. A
reader takes that as a product surface, not as an undocumented endpoint. The gap is therefore
either:

1. a **feature gap** — the explain verdict should be reachable from the UI (most likely from
   a record page, for an admin or a user holding the relevant admin permission); or
2. a **docs wording issue** — "audit and explain" should say that explain is an API-level
   capability.

Filing it as one issue because the right resolution is a product decision, not a reporter's
guess. This report registers the observation only; it prescribes no implementation.

## Impact

- Admins debugging "why can/can't this person see this" have no in-product path.
- The strongest part of the permission model is invisible to the people it was built for.
- Anything that wants to *show* the model (documentation, onboarding, a walkthrough) has to
  build its own renderer. That is exactly what happened here: the walkthrough had to render
  the raw API response as a graphic card, with an explicit
  `GET /api/v1/security/explain` provenance line and a "Rendered from live API response"
  footnote, because there was nothing in the product to point a camera at.

## Related observation (separate, smaller)

When an object's API name is misspelled, `explain` reports `denies` rather than an
"unknown object" error — a wrong object name and a genuine denial are indistinguishable in the
response. Recorded here for context; happy to split it into its own issue if preferred.

## Provenance

Registered during production of steedos-labs/video-studio#3 (permissions walkthrough) on
2026-08-20 as finding **P-1**, marked "registered, pending transfer". The transfer was never
made; this issue closes that loop. No duplicate was found in this repository
(searched for explain / permission-decision / UI-surfacing issues before filing).
